**Chinese name:** 紫光展锐（上海）科技有限公司 (Zǐguāng Zhǎnruì (Shànghǎi) Kējì Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Part of Tsinghua Unigroup (the same state-linked group behind YMTC), formed from the 2018 merger of Spreadtrum Communications (founded 2001) and RDA Microelectronics — one of the highest-volume mobile chipset vendors globally by unit shipments, concentrated in the mass market rather than flagship tier. The fourth-largest smartphone SoC vendor worldwide per Counterpoint, behind MediaTek, Qualcomm and Apple, with 12.1% share for full-year 2025 and 14% in Q1 2026; FY2025 revenue was ~¥20 billion (first time above that mark, up from ¥14.5 billion in 2024). IPO: sponsors 国泰海通+中信建投 filed the third tutoring-progress report in April 2026 (prospectus framework and filing drafts reportedly assembled), but as of 11 October 2026 no SSE acceptance or published prospectus had occurred.
:::

## What does this firm design?

Mobile SoCs and baseband chipsets for entry-level and mid-range smartphones, plus IoT and automotive chip lines — a global top-two player in sub-$99 smartphone silicon, with Transsion its largest customer. The 6nm T8300 (launched March 2025, benchmarking >510k) was its first SoC integrating 5G NR NTN satellite communications, first shipped in nubia's Neo 3 gaming phones; 5G handsets on UNISOC silicon ship to 76+ countries.
